<!--
IMPORTANT — see MAGIC-MOVE-NOTES.md / the compatibility report from the
Part B investigation (Julia + JS libraries): none of the sequences below
currently animate.

magic-move.js's initSvgMagicMove() runs once, synchronously, on Reveal's
`ready` event (_extensions/magic-move/magic-move.js ~line 16-19), and
decides `slide._hasSvgContent` (~line 560) and groups slides into
`_svgMagicSequence`s (~line 573, groupConsecutiveSvgSlides) at that single
point in time. Quarto's {ojs} cells are evaluated by the Observable
runtime asynchronously *after* Reveal.initialize() resolves and `ready`
fires — the <svg> a Plot/D3/Vega-Lite cell produces is not yet in the DOM
when magic-move looks for it. Verified empirically (Playwright, 3/3 runs):
`section._hasSvgContent` is `false` and no `_svgMagicSequence` is ever
assigned, even though the real inline <svg> is present in the DOM moments
later. This is a structural timing race in the extension, not a property
of any specific charting library — it reproduces identically for
Observable Plot, raw D3, and Vega-Lite/vega-embed.

Kept as a demonstration of what real ojs-rendered SVG DOM looks like
(inspected with Playwright: Plot -> <circle>/<path>/<text>, D3 -> literal
<circle>/<rect>, Vega-Lite via vega-embed(renderer: "svg") -> <path>/
<line>/<text>), in case a future fix re-scans for SVG content after ojs
settles. No Playwright morph tests were added for this file since there is
currently no morph to test — see the Part B write-up for details.
-->

## Not Yet Supported

None of the sequences on this page currently animate — every transition
below **hard-cuts** instead of morphing. D3, Observable Plot, and
Vega-Lite (via `{ojs}`) all produce fully compatible SVG shapes
(`<circle>`, `<rect>`, `<path>`, `<line>`, `<text>`), but Quarto's
Observable JS cells render *after* Reveal's `ready` event, while this
extension only scans for SVG content once, synchronously, at `ready`. So
the SVG magic-move feature never activates for `{ojs}`-rendered charts,
regardless of shape compatibility. Kept here as a reference for what
real `{ojs}`-rendered SVG looks like, pending a fix upstream.

## D3 Shapes - Position 1 {.magic-move}

```{ojs}
{
  const svg = d3.create("svg").attr("width", 400).attr("height", 300);
  svg.append("circle").attr("cx", 80).attr("cy", 80).attr("r", 30).attr("fill", "steelblue");
  svg.append("rect").attr("x", 200).attr("y", 180).attr("width", 60).attr("height", 40).attr("fill", "coral");
  return svg.node();
}
```

## D3 Shapes - Position 2 {.magic-move}

```{ojs}
{
  const svg = d3.create("svg").attr("width", 400).attr("height", 300);
  svg.append("circle").attr("cx", 300).attr("cy", 200).attr("r", 50).attr("fill", "steelblue");
  svg.append("rect").attr("x", 40).attr("y", 40).attr("width", 100).attr("height", 25).attr("fill", "coral");
```

## Observable Plot - Dots Low {.magic-move}

```{ojs}
Plot.plot({
  width: 500,
  height: 350,
  marks: [
    Plot.dot([{x: 1, y: 1}, {x: 2, y: 1.2}, {x: 3, y: 1}], {x: "x", y: "y", r: 10, fill: "steelblue"})
  ]
})
```

```{ojs}

    Plot.dot([{x: 1, y: 3}, {x: 2, y: 3.5}, {x: 3, y: 3}], {x: "x", y: "y", r: 10, fill: "steelblue"})
```

## Vega-Lite Points - Layout 1 {.magic-move}

```{ojs}
//| output: false
vegaEmbed = require("vega-embed@6")
```

```{ojs}
//| output: false
vlSpecA = ({
  $schema: "https://vega.github.io/schema/vega-lite/v5.json",
  width: 400,
  height: 300,
  data: {values: [{x: 1, y: 1}, {x: 2, y: 3}, {x: 3, y: 2}]},
  mark: "point",
  encoding: {
    x: {field: "x", type: "quantitative"},
    y: {field: "y", type: "quantitative"}
  }
})
```

```{ojs}
{
  const div = document.createElement("div");
  await vegaEmbed(div, vlSpecA, {renderer: "svg", actions: false});
  return div;
}
```
